+// Test fixture for issue 745 — nested-structs rule
+// must not report on Go "set" patterns inside interface declarations,
+// while still flagging genuine nested-struct usages outside interfaces.
+package fixtures
+
+// Bug case from issue 745: interface method returning map[string]struct{}
+// must NOT trigger a failure.
+type mySetInterface interface {
+	GetSet() map[string]struct{}
+}
+
+var _ mySetInterface
+
+// Named empty struct used as map value inside an interface method.
+type emptyType struct{}
+
+type myTypedSetInterface interface {
+	GetSet() map[string]emptyType
+}
+
+var _ myTypedSetInterface
+
+// Interface method returning a non-empty struct nested inline.
+// Reference skips entire interface declarations, so even this is NOT flagged.
+type myInlineStructInterface interface {
+	GetStruct() struct{ b bool }
+}
+
+var _ myInlineStructInterface
+
+// Simple interface with no struct types — must not trigger.
+type SimpleInterface interface {
+	Foo() int
+}
+
+var _ SimpleInterface
+
+// Struct method returning a Go-set: this already worked in BASE
+// (FuncDecl bodies only get walked, not signatures) — preservation.
+type mySetStruct struct{}
+
+func (mySetStruct) GetSet() map[string]struct{} {
+	return map[string]struct{}{}
+}
+
+var _ mySetStruct
+
+// Preservation: regular nested struct inside a struct field must still be flagged.
+type outer struct {
+	Inner struct { // MATCH /no nested structs are allowed/
+		x int
+	}
+}
+
+// Preservation (issue 664): a slice of empty structs as a struct field
+// must still be flagged.
+type sliceOfEmpty struct {
+	Items []struct{} // MATCH /no nested structs are allowed/
+}
+
+// Preservation: map[string]struct{} as a regular struct field
+// is still flagged by the reference (the fix is narrow — only interface
+// declarations are skipped).
+type mapInStruct struct {
+	data map[string]struct{} // MATCH /no nested structs are allowed/
+}
+
+// Preservation (issue 744): channel of empty struct must NOT be flagged.
+type channelStruct struct {
+	c chan struct{}
+}
+
+// Preservation: function-typed struct field whose signature contains a
+// non-empty struct is still flagged by the reference. The fix is narrow —
+// only interface declarations are skipped, not function-typed struct fields.
+type funcFieldStruct struct {
+	handler func() struct{ b bool } // MATCH /no nested structs are allowed/
+}

import re

source = open(sys.argv[2]).read().splitlines(True)
out = []
i = 0
while i < len(source):
    line = source[i]
    m = re.match(r"(test\(['\"])(.*?)(['\"],\s*t\s*=>\s*\{)", line)
    if not m:
        out.append(line)
        i += 1
        continue
    block = [line]
    depth = line.count('{') - line.count('}')
    i += 1
    while i < len(source) and depth > 0:
        block.append(source[i])
        depth += source[i].count('{') - source[i].count('}')
        i += 1
    if pattern.match(m.group(2)):
        out.extend(block)
open(sys.argv[3], 'w').writelines(out)
PY

+def _title_on_axes(ax, title):
+    """True if the title text is rendered on the given axes via either
+    `set_title` (axes.get_title) or `text2D`/`text` (axes.texts)."""
+    if ax.get_title() == title:
+        return True
+    for txt in ax.texts:
+        if txt.get_text() == title:
+            return True
+    return False
+
+
+def _suptitle_text(fig):
+    """Return the figure's current suptitle text, or None."""
+    if fig._suptitle is None:
+        return None
+    return fig._suptitle.get_text()
+
+
+def test_plot_surf_title_on_axes_no_axes_provided():
+    """plot_surf(title=...) without `axes`: the title must be visible on
+    the figure -- either on the axes or as the figure's suptitle (both
+    are valid in this no-subplot scenario)."""
+    mesh = generate_surf()
+    display = plot_surf(mesh, title='Test title', engine='matplotlib')
+    assert (
+        _title_on_axes(display.axes[0], 'Test title')
+        or _suptitle_text(display) == 'Test title'
+    )
+    plt.close('all')
+
+
+def test_plot_surf_stat_map_title_on_axes_no_axes_provided():
+    """plot_surf_stat_map(title=...) without `axes`: the title must be
+    visible somewhere on the figure."""
+    mesh = generate_surf()
+    rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
+    data = 10 * rng.standard_normal(size=mesh[0].shape[0])
+    display = plot_surf_stat_map(mesh, stat_map=data, title='Stat map title')
+    assert (
+        _title_on_axes(display.axes[0], 'Stat map title')
+        or _suptitle_text(display) == 'Stat map title'
+    )
+    plt.close('all')
+
+
+def test_plot_surf_stat_map_subplots_each_axes_has_own_title():
+    """Issue scenario: two subplots each given their own title via
+    `plot_surf_stat_map(..., title=..., axes=...)`. Each subplot's
+    axes must carry its own title (either as get_title or in axes.texts),
+    and the figure suptitle must not carry either of those titles --
+    otherwise the second call would clobber the first via suptitle.
+    Distinct titles per subplot guard against coincidental-correctness."""
+    mesh = generate_surf()
+    rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
+    data = 10 * rng.standard_normal(size=mesh[0].shape[0])
+    fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows=1, ncols=2,
+                             subplot_kw={'projection': '3d'})
+    plot_surf_stat_map(mesh, stat_map=data,
+                       title='a subplot', axes=axes[0])
+    plot_surf_stat_map(mesh, stat_map=data,
+                       title='an other subplot', axes=axes[1])
+    assert _title_on_axes(axes[0], 'a subplot')
+    assert _title_on_axes(axes[1], 'an other subplot')
+    sup = _suptitle_text(fig)
+    assert sup != 'a subplot'
+    assert sup != 'an other subplot'
+    plt.close('all')
+
+
+def test_plot_surf_stat_map_title_on_axes_when_axes_provided():
+    """plot_surf_stat_map(title=..., axes=ax): the title must appear on
+    the provided axes and not as the figure's suptitle."""
+    mesh = generate_surf()
+    rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
+    data = 10 * rng.standard_normal(size=mesh[0].shape[0])
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(subplot_kw={'projection': '3d'})
+    plot_surf_stat_map(mesh, stat_map=data,
+                       title='single subplot title', axes=ax)
+    assert _title_on_axes(ax, 'single subplot title')
+    assert _suptitle_text(fig) != 'single subplot title'
+    plt.close('all')
+
+
+def test_plot_surf_roi_title_on_axes_when_axes_provided():
+    """plot_surf_roi(title=..., axes=ax): the title must appear on the
+    provided axes and not as the figure's suptitle."""
+    mesh = generate_surf()
+    roi_map = np.zeros(mesh[0].shape[0])
+    roi_map[:10] = 1
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(subplot_kw={'projection': '3d'})
+    plot_surf_roi(mesh, roi_map=roi_map,

+    plt.close('all')
+
+
+def test_plot_surf_contours_title_on_axes_when_axes_provided():
+    """plot_surf_contours(title=..., axes=ax, legend=True): the title

+    leave plot_surf_contours still calling figure.suptitle."""

+package handshake
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+
+	"github.com/lucas-clemente/quic-go/internal/protocol"
+
+	. "github.com/onsi/ginkgo"
+	. "github.com/onsi/gomega"
+)
+
+var _ = Describe("Transport Parameters original_connection_id", func() {
+	It("round-trips the original connection ID through marshaling", func() {
+		connID := protocol.ConnectionID{0xde, 0xad, 0xbe, 0xef}
+		params := &TransportParameters{
+			InitialMaxData:       0x4321,
+			StatelessResetToken:  bytes.Repeat([]byte{0x42}, 16),
+			OriginalConnectionID: connID,
+		}
+		b := &bytes.Buffer{}
+		params.marshal(b)
+
+		p := &TransportParameters{}
+		Expect(p.unmarshal(b.Bytes(), protocol.PerspectiveServer)).To(Succeed())
+		Expect(p.OriginalConnectionID).To(Equal(connID))
+
+		Expect(p.InitialMaxData).To(Equal(protocol.ByteCount(0x4321)))
+	})
+
+	It("leaves the original connection ID empty when none was sent", func() {
+		params := &TransportParameters{
+			InitialMaxData:      0x1234,
+			StatelessResetToken: bytes.Repeat([]byte{0x42}, 16),
+		}
+		b := &bytes.Buffer{}
+		params.marshal(b)
+
+		p := &TransportParameters{}
+		Expect(p.unmarshal(b.Bytes(), protocol.PerspectiveServer)).To(Succeed())
+		Expect(p.OriginalConnectionID).To(BeEmpty())
+	})
+
+	It("rejects an original_connection_id sent by a client", func() {
+		params := &TransportParameters{
+			OriginalConnectionID: protocol.ConnectionID{0xca, 0xfe},
+		}
+		b := &bytes.Buffer{}
+		params.marshal(b)
+
+		p := &TransportParameters{}
+		err := p.unmarshal(b.Bytes(), protocol.PerspectiveClient)
+		Expect(err).To(HaveOccurred())
+		Expect(err.Error()).To(ContainSubstring("original_connection_id"))
+	})
+
+	It("accepts an original_connection_id sent by a server", func() {
+		params := &TransportParameters{
+			OriginalConnectionID: protocol.ConnectionID{0xca, 0xfe},
+			StatelessResetToken:  bytes.Repeat([]byte{0x42}, 16),
+		}
+		b := &bytes.Buffer{}
+		params.marshal(b)
+
+		p := &TransportParameters{}
+		Expect(p.unmarshal(b.Bytes(), protocol.PerspectiveServer)).To(Succeed())
+		Expect(p.OriginalConnectionID).To(Equal(protocol.ConnectionID{0xca, 0xfe}))
+	})
+
+	It("includes the original connection ID in the string representation", func() {
+		connID := protocol.ConnectionID{0xde, 0xad, 0xbe, 0xef}
+		withID := (&TransportParameters{OriginalConnectionID: connID}).String()
+		Expect(withID).To(ContainSubstring(connID.String()))
+
+		withoutID := (&TransportParameters{}).String()
+		Expect(withoutID).ToNot(ContainSubstring(connID.String()))
+	})
+})

+import struct
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+
+from tritonclient.utils import (
+    InferenceServerException,
+    deserialize_bf16_tensor,
+    deserialize_bytes_tensor,
+    serialize_byte_tensor,
+)
+
+
+def _encoded(*values):
+    return b"".join(struct.pack("<I", len(value)) + value for value in values)
+
+
+def test_bytes_deserializer_accepts_buffer_protocol_and_preserves_payloads():
+    encoded = _encoded(b"a\x00b", b"", bytes(range(8)))
+    expected = np.array([b"a\x00b", b"", bytes(range(8))], dtype=object)
+    for buffer in (encoded, bytearray(encoded), memoryview(encoded)):
+        actual = deserialize_bytes_tensor(buffer)
+        assert actual.dtype == np.object_
+        assert actual.tolist() == expected.tolist()
+
+
+def test_bytes_deserializer_empty_payload_is_empty_object_array():
+    result = deserialize_bytes_tensor(b"")
+    assert result.dtype == np.object_
+    assert result.shape == (0,)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "payload",
+    [
+        b"\x01\x00\x00",
+        struct.pack("<I", 4) + b"abc",
+        _encoded(b"ok") + b"\x00",
+    ],
+)
+def test_bytes_deserializer_rejects_malformed_framing(payload):
+    with pytest.raises(InferenceServerException):
+        deserialize_bytes_tensor(payload)
+
+
+def test_bytes_deserializer_rejects_non_buffer_input():
+    with pytest.raises(InferenceServerException):
+        deserialize_bytes_tensor([1, 2, 3, 4])
+
+
+def test_bf16_deserializer_accepts_buffer_protocol_and_decodes_values():
+    source = np.array([0.0, 1.0, -2.5, np.inf], dtype=np.float32)
+    encoded = b"".join(struct.pack("<f", value)[2:4] for value in source)
+    for buffer in (encoded, bytearray(encoded), memoryview(encoded)):
+        actual = deserialize_bf16_tensor(buffer)
+        assert actual.dtype == np.float32
+        assert actual.ndim == 1
+        assert np.allclose(actual, source, equal_nan=True)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("payload", [b"\x00", b"\x00\x00\x00"])
+def test_bf16_deserializer_rejects_non_element_aligned_payload(payload):
+    with pytest.raises(InferenceServerException):
+        deserialize_bf16_tensor(payload)
+
+
+def test_bf16_deserializer_rejects_non_buffer_input():
+    with pytest.raises(InferenceServerException):
+        deserialize_bf16_tensor([0, 1])
+
+
+def test_byte_serializer_preserves_bytes_like_objects_in_c_order():
+    values = np.empty((2, 3), dtype=object)
+    values.flat[:] = [
+        memoryview(b"first\x00"),
+        bytearray(b"second"),
+        b"",
+        b"third",
+        np.bytes_(b"fourth"),
+        b"last",
+    ]
+    encoded = serialize_byte_tensor(values).item()
+    assert encoded == _encoded(
+        b"first\x00", b"second", b"", b"third", b"fourth", b"last"
+    )

@@ -0,0 +1,90 @@
+
+
+
+
+
+package translator
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"testing"
+
+	extprocv3 "github.com/envoyproxy/go-control-plane/envoy/service/ext_proc/v3"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+	"github.com/tidwall/gjson"
+
+	"github.com/envoyproxy/ai-gateway/internal/apischema/openai"
+)
+
+func translatedVertexBody(t *testing.T, request string) (map[string]any, string) {
+	t.Helper()
+	var input openai.ChatCompletionRequest
+	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(request), &input))
+	header, body, err := NewChatCompletionOpenAIToGCPVertexAITranslator("").RequestBody(nil, &input, false)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotNil(t, header)
+	require.NotNil(t, body)
+	var payload map[string]any
+	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(body.GetMutation().(*extprocv3.BodyMutation_Body).Body, &payload))
+	path := ""
+	for _, h := range header.SetHeaders {
+		if h.Header.Key == ":path" {
+			path = string(h.Header.RawValue)
+		}
+	}
+	return payload, path
+}
+
+func TestVertexSafetySettingsForwardingContract(t *testing.T) {
+	payload, path := translatedVertexBody(t, `{
+		"model": "gemini-2.0-flash",
+		"temperature": 0.4,
+		"max_tokens": 256,
+		"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "classify this"}],
+		"generationConfig": {"thinkingConfig": {"includeThoughts": true, "thinkingBudget": 128}},
+		"safetySettings": [
+			{"category": "HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH", "threshold": "BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE"},
+			{"method": "SEVERITY", "category": "HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT", "threshold": "BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH"}
+		]
+	}`)
+	require.Equal(t, "publishers/google/models/gemini-2.0-flash:generateContent", path)
+	bodyJSON := string(mustJSON(t, payload))
+	require.Equal(t, float64(0.4), gjson.Get(bodyJSON, "generation_config.temperature").Float())
+	require.Equal(t, float64(256), gjson.Get(bodyJSON, "generation_config.maxOutputTokens").Float())
+	require.True(t, gjson.Get(bodyJSON, "generation_config.thinkingConfig.includeThoughts").Bool())
+	safety := gjson.Get(bodyJSON, "safetySettings")
+	require.Len(t, safety.Array(), 2)
+	require.Equal(t, "HARM_CATEGORY_HATE_SPEECH", safety.Get("0.category").String())
+	require.Equal(t, "BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE", safety.Get("0.threshold").String())
+	require.Equal(t, "SEVERITY", safety.Get("1.method").String())
+	require.Equal(t, "HARM_CATEGORY_DANGEROUS_CONTENT", safety.Get("1.category").String())
+	require.Equal(t, "BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH", safety.Get("1.threshold").String())
+}
+
+func TestVertexSafetySettingsStreamingContract(t *testing.T) {
+	payload, path := translatedVertexBody(t, `{
+		"model": "gemini-2.0-flash",
+		"stream": true,
+		"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "stream this"}],
+		"safetySettings": [{"category": "HARM_CATEGORY_HARASSMENT", "threshold": "BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE"}]
+	}`)
+	require.Equal(t, "publishers/google/models/gemini-2.0-flash:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse", path)
+	bodyJSON := string(mustJSON(t, payload))
+	require.Equal(t, "HARM_CATEGORY_HARASSMENT", gjson.Get(bodyJSON, "safetySettings.0.category").String())
+	require.Equal(t, "BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE", gjson.Get(bodyJSON, "safetySettings.0.threshold").String())
+}
+
+func TestVertexSafetySettingsOmissionContract(t *testing.T) {
+	withoutVendor, _ := translatedVertexBody(t, `{
+		"model": "gemini-2.0-flash",
+		"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "ordinary request"}]
+	}`)
+	require.False(t, gjson.Get(string(mustJSON(t, withoutVendor)), "safetySettings").Exists())
+}
+
+func mustJSON(t *testing.T, value map[string]any) []byte {
+	t.Helper()
+	b, err := json.Marshal(value)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	return b
+}

+const assert = require('assert')
+const defaultsDeep = require('./defaultsDeep')
+
+describe('defaultsDeep presence predicate', () => {
+  it('keeps the documented nullish default behavior when omitted', () => {
+    assert.deepEqual(
+      defaultsDeep({ count: 1, nested: { enabled: true } })({ count: null }),
+      { count: 1, nested: { enabled: true } },
+    )
+  })
+
+  it('retains values accepted by a custom predicate, including falsy values', () => {
+    const input = { zero: 0, no: false, empty: '', nil: null, nested: { value: 7 } }
+    const isPresent = () => true
+    assert.deepEqual(
+      defaultsDeep({ zero: 9, no: true, empty: 'fallback', nil: 'fallback', nested: { value: 8 } }, isPresent)(input),
+      input,
+    )
+  })
+
+  it('uses defaults when the predicate rejects a value', () => {
+    const isPresent = value => value !== 0 && value !== ''
+    assert.deepEqual(
+      defaultsDeep({ count: 3, label: 'fallback' }, isPresent)({ count: 0, label: '' }),
+      { count: 3, label: 'fallback' },
+    )
+  })
+
+  it('applies the predicate recursively through accepted object branches', () => {
+    const isPresent = value => value !== null && value !== undefined && value !== 0
+    assert.deepEqual(
+      defaultsDeep({ profile: { score: 10, name: 'guest' } }, isPresent)(
+        { profile: { score: 0 } },
+      ),
+      { profile: { score: 10, name: 'guest' } },
+    )
+  })
+
+  it('replaces a rejected nested branch instead of merging its children', () => {
+    const isPresent = value => value !== false
+    assert.deepEqual(
+      defaultsDeep({ settings: { enabled: true, mode: 'safe' } }, isPresent)(
+        { settings: false },
+      ),
+      { settings: { enabled: true, mode: 'safe' } },
+    )
+  })
+
+  it('handles array slots independently and preserves extra input slots', () => {
+    const isPresent = value => value !== null && value !== undefined && value !== 0
+    assert.deepEqual(
+      defaultsDeep([1, { x: 2, y: 3 }, 4], isPresent)([0, { x: 0 }, 9]),
+      [1, { x: 2, y: 3 }, 9],
+    )
+    assert.deepEqual(
+      defaultsDeep([1, 2], isPresent)([0, 8, 9]),
+      [1, 8, 9],
+    )
+  })
+
+  it('returns nullish and non-collection inputs unchanged', () => {
+    const isPresent = () => false
+    assert.strictEqual(defaultsDeep({ a: 1 }, isPresent)(null), null)
+    assert.strictEqual(defaultsDeep({ a: 1 }, isPresent)(undefined), undefined)
+    assert.strictEqual(defaultsDeep({ a: 1 }, isPresent)(42), 42)
+  })
+
+  it('does not mutate the source and propagates predicate errors', () => {
+    const input = { nested: { count: 0 } }
+    const result = defaultsDeep({ nested: { count: 1 } }, value => value !== 0)(input)
+    assert.deepEqual(result, { nested: { count: 1 } })
+    assert.deepEqual(input, { nested: { count: 0 } })
+    assert.throws(
+      () => defaultsDeep({ a: 1 }, () => { throw new Error('presence failure') })({ a: 2 }),
+      /presence failure/,
+    )
+  })
+})

+package schema_test
+
+import (
+	"io/ioutil"
+	"os"
+	"reflect"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+
+	config "github.com/GoogleContainerTools/skaffold/pkg/skaffold/config"
+	"github.com/GoogleContainerTools/skaffold/pkg/skaffold/schema"
+	"github.com/GoogleContainerTools/skaffold/pkg/skaffold/schema/latest"
+	yaml "gopkg.in/yaml.v2"
+)
+
+const profileRequiresBase = `apiVersion: skaffold/v1beta10
+kind: Config
+build:
+  artifacts:
+  - image: original
+    docker:
+      dockerfile: Original
+`
+
+func parseProfileRequiresConfig(t *testing.T, profiles string) *latest.SkaffoldConfig {
+	t.Helper()
+	f, err := ioutil.TempFile("", "profile-requires-*.yaml")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	name := f.Name()
+	defer os.Remove(name)
+	if _, err := f.WriteString(profileRequiresBase + profiles); err != nil {
+		f.Close()
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if err := f.Close(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+
+	parsed, err := schema.ParseConfig(name, false)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("expected the latest profile schema to accept requires: %v", err)
+	}
+	return parsed.(*latest.SkaffoldConfig)
+}
+
+func profileRequiresImages(c *latest.SkaffoldConfig) []string {
+	var images []string
+	for _, artifact := range c.Build.Artifacts {
+		images = append(images, artifact.ImageName)
+	}
+	return images
+}
+
+func profileRequiresPipeline(t *testing.T, c *latest.SkaffoldConfig) string {
+	t.Helper()
+	b, err := yaml.Marshal(c.Pipeline)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	return string(b)
+}
+
+func requireProfileErrorNames(t *testing.T, err error, names ...string) {
+	t.Helper()
+	if err == nil {
+		t.Fatal("expected profile dependency resolution to fail")
+	}

+import os
+import shutil
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+
+from pulp.plugins.util.publish_step import AtomicDirectoryPublishStep
+
+
+class Parent(object):
+    def __init__(self, timestamp):
+        self.timestamp = timestamp
+
+
+def write_file(path, content):
+    parent = os.path.dirname(path)
+    if not os.path.exists(parent):
+        os.makedirs(parent)
+    with open(path, 'w') as handle:
+        handle.write(content)
+
+
+class AtomicDirectoryContractTests(unittest.TestCase):
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.root = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='pulp-atomic-contract-')
+        self.source = os.path.join(self.root, 'source')
+        self.master = os.path.join(self.root, 'master')
+        self.published = os.path.join(self.root, 'published')
+        os.makedirs(self.source)
+        os.makedirs(self.master)
+        os.makedirs(self.published)
+
+    def tearDown(self):
+        shutil.rmtree(self.root)
+
+    def make_step(self, locations, contents=False, timestamp='publish-001'):
+        step = AtomicDirectoryPublishStep(
+            self.source, locations, self.master,
+            only_publish_directory_contents=contents)
+        step.parent = Parent(timestamp)

+
+

+MESSAGE = "Don't use pd.array in core, import array as pd_array instead"
+
+
+class TestUsePdArrayContract(unittest.TestCase):
+    def run_validator(self, files):
+        return subprocess.run(
+            [sys.executable, str(SCRIPT), *(str(path) for path in files)],
+            cwd=REPO_ROOT,
+            check=False,
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+        )
+
+    def test_reports_each_real_pandas_array_use_and_import(self):
+        content = "\n".join(
+            [
+                "import pandas as pd",
+                "import pandas",
+                "import pandas as p",
+                "import pandas.core as core",
+                "import unrelated as other",
+                "value1 = pd.array",
+                "value2 = pandas.array",
+                "value3 = p.array",
+                "value4 = core.array",
+                "value5 = other.array",
+                "from pandas import array",
+                "from pandas import array as arr",
+                "from pandas import array as pd_array",
+                "from unrelated import array",
+            ]
+        )
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
+            path = pathlib.Path(directory) / "aliases.py"
+            path.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
+            result = self.run_validator([path])
+
+        expected = "\n".join(
+            [
+                f"{path}:6:9: {MESSAGE}",
+                f"{path}:7:9: {MESSAGE}",
+                f"{path}:8:9: {MESSAGE}",
+                f"{path}:11:0: {MESSAGE}",
+                f"{path}:12:0: {MESSAGE}",
+                "",
+            ]
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
+        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, expected)
+
+    def test_unrelated_names_are_not_reported(self):
+        content = "\n".join(

+                "pd = object()",
+                "first = pd.array",

+package openapi3filter_test
+
+import (
+	"archive/zip"
+	"bytes"
+	"context"
+	"fmt"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+
+	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3"
+	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/openapi3filter"
+	"github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/routers/gorillamux"
+)
+
+type zipEntry struct {
+	Name string
+	Body string
+}
+
+func TestValidateApplicationZipRequestBodyUsesDefaultDecoder(t *testing.T) {
+	body := makeZipArchive(t, zipEntry{Name: "entry.txt", Body: "alpha-one"})
+
+	err := validateZipRequestBody(t, `pattern: "^alpha-"`, body)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+}
+
+func TestValidateApplicationZipRequestBodyUsesDecodedFileContent(t *testing.T) {
+	tests := []struct {
+		name           string
+		schemaFragment string
+		entries        []zipEntry
+		wantErr        bool
+	}{
+		{
+			name:           "alpha content matches alpha schema",
+			schemaFragment: `pattern: "^alpha-"`,
+			entries:        []zipEntry{{Name: "alpha.txt", Body: "alpha-two"}},
+		},
+		{
+			name:           "beta content matches beta schema",
+			schemaFragment: `pattern: "^beta-"`,
+			entries:        []zipEntry{{Name: "beta.txt", Body: "beta-three"}},
+		},
+		{
+			name:           "decoded content is still schema validated",
+			schemaFragment: `pattern: "^beta-"`,
+			entries:        []zipEntry{{Name: "gamma.txt", Body: "gamma-four"}},
+			wantErr:        true,
+		},
+	}
+
+	for _, tt := range tests {
+		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			body := makeZipArchive(t, tt.entries...)
+
+			err := validateZipRequestBody(t, tt.schemaFragment, body)
+			if tt.wantErr {
+				require.Error(t, err)
+				return
+			}
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+func TestZipFileBodyDecoderReadsArchiveContent(t *testing.T) {
+	body := makeZipArchive(t,
+		zipEntry{Name: "first.txt", Body: "first-token"},
+		zipEntry{Name: "second.txt", Body: "second-token"},
+	)
+
+	value, err := openapi3filter.ZipFileBodyDecoder(bytes.NewReader(body), nil, nil, nil)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	decoded, ok := value.(string)
+	require.True(t, ok, "decoded zip body should be a string")
+	require.Contains(t, decoded, "first-token")
+	require.Contains(t, decoded, "second-token")
+}
+
+func TestInvalidApplicationZipBodyFailsAsZipDecodeError(t *testing.T) {
+	tests := [][]byte{
+		[]byte("not a zip archive"),
+		{0x50, 0x4b, 0x03, 0x04, 0x01},
+	}
+
+	for _, body := range tests {
+		err := validateZipRequestBody(t, `minLength: 1`, body)
+		require.Error(t, err)
+		requireNotUnsupportedZipDecoderError(t, err)
+
+		_, err = openapi3filter.ZipFileBodyDecoder(bytes.NewReader(body), nil, nil, nil)
+		require.Error(t, err)
+	}
+}
+
+func requireNotUnsupportedZipDecoderError(t *testing.T, err error) {
+	t.Helper()
+
+	msg := strings.ToLower(err.Error())
+	require.NotContains(t, msg, "no body decoder")
+	require.False(t,
+		strings.Contains(msg, "unsupported") &&
+			(strings.Contains(msg, "application/zip") ||
+				strings.Contains(msg, "content type") ||
+				strings.Contains(msg, "media type") ||
+				strings.Contains(msg, "decoder")),
+		"error should come from zip decoding, not unsupported application/zip attribution: %v", err)
+	require.False(t,
+		strings.Contains(msg, "missing") && strings.Contains(msg, "decoder"),
+		"error should come from zip decoding, not a missing decoder: %v", err)
+}
+
+func validateZipRequestBody(t *testing.T, schemaFragment string, body []byte) error {
+	t.Helper()
+
+	spec := fmt.Sprintf(`
+openapi: 3.0.0
+info:
+  title: 'Validator'
+  version: 0.0.1
+paths:
+  /zip:
+    post:
+      requestBody:
+        required: true
+        content:
+          application/zip:
+            schema:
+              type: string
+              %s
+      responses:
+        '200':
+          description: OK
+`, schemaFragment)
+
+	loader := openapi3.NewLoader()
+	doc, err := loader.LoadFromData([]byte(spec))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NoError(t, doc.Validate(loader.Context))
+
+	router, err := gorillamux.NewRouter(doc)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	req := newZipRequest(t, body)
+
+	route, pathParams, err := router.FindRoute(req)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	return openapi3filter.ValidateRequestBody(
+		context.Background(),
+		&openapi3filter.RequestValidationInput{
+			Request:    req,
+			PathParams: pathParams,
+			Route:      route,
+		},
+		route.Operation.RequestBody.Value,
+	)
+}
+
+func newZipRequest(t *testing.T, body []byte) *http.Request {
+	t.Helper()
+
+	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/zip", bytes.NewReader(body))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/zip")
+	return req
+}
+
+func makeZipArchive(t *testing.T, entries ...zipEntry) []byte {
+	t.Helper()
+
+	var body bytes.Buffer
+	zw := zip.NewWriter(&body)
+	for _, entry := range entries {
+		w, err := zw.Create(entry.Name)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		_, err = w.Write([]byte(entry.Body))
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+	}
+	require.NoError(t, zw.Close())
+	return body.Bytes()
+}

+import pytest
+
+from celery import Celery, states
+from celery.exceptions import IncompleteStream
+from celery.utils.graph import GraphFormatter
+
+
+class RequestWithChildren:
+    def __init__(self, children):
+        self.children = children
+
+
+def make_app(name):
+    app = Celery(name, broker="memory://", backend="cache+memory://")
+    app.conf.result_serializer = "json"
+    app.conf.accept_content = ["json"]
+    return app
+
+
+def store_success(app, task_id, value, children=None):
+    request = RequestWithChildren(children or [])
+    app.backend.store_result(task_id, value, states.SUCCESS, request=request)
+
+
+def collect_ids(result, **kwargs):
+    return [(handle.id, value) for handle, value in result.collect(**kwargs)]
+
+
+def dependency_ids(result, **kwargs):
+    return [(parent and parent.id, node.id) for parent, node in result.iterdeps(**kwargs)]
+
+
+def graph_edges(graph):
+    return {
+        (node.id, child.id)
+        for node in graph
+        for child in graph[node]
+    }
+

+
+
+

+    ]:

+    children = [
+        app.AsyncResult("s3-child0"),
+        app.AsyncResult("s3-child1"),
+        app.AsyncResult("s3-child2"),
+    ]
+    store_success(app, "s3-root", "root-value", children=children)
+
+    root = app.AsyncResult("s3-root")
+
+    assert dependency_ids(root) == [
+        (None, "s3-root"),
+        ("s3-root", "s3-child0"),
+        ("s3-root", "s3-child1"),
+        ("s3-root", "s3-child2"),
+    ]
+    assert collect_ids(root, disable_sync_subtasks=False) == [
+        ("s3-root", "root-value"),
+        ("s3-child0", 0),
+        ("s3-child1", 1),
+        ("s3-child2", 2),
+    ]
+
+    assert [node_id for _, node_id in dependency_ids(root)][1:] == [
+        "s3-child0", "s3-child1", "s3-child2",
+    ]
+
+
+def test_get_leaf_returns_last_result_value_from_simple_chain():
+
+
+
+    app = make_app("fixture-chain-leaf")
+    store_success(app, "s3-chain-leaf", 2)
+    store_success(
+        app,
+        "s3-chain-middle",

+        "chain-root-value",
+        children=[app.AsyncResult("s3-chain-middle")],
+    )
+
+    root = app.AsyncResult("s3-chain-root")
+
+    assert dependency_ids(root) == [
+        (None, "s3-chain-root"),
+        ("s3-chain-root", "s3-chain-middle"),
+        ("s3-chain-middle", "s3-chain-leaf"),
+    ]
+    assert root.get_leaf() == 2
+
+
+def test_nested_ready_tree_uses_breadth_first_order_for_collect_and_leaf():
+
+
+
+    app = make_app("fixture-nested-ready")
+    store_success(app, "s3-aa", "AA")
+    store_success(app, "s3-bb", "BB")
+    store_success(app, "s3-a", "A", children=[app.AsyncResult("s3-aa")])
+    store_success(app, "s3-b", "B", children=[app.AsyncResult("s3-bb")])
+    store_success(
+        app,
+        "s3-bf-root",
+        "ROOT",
+        children=[app.AsyncResult("s3-a"), app.AsyncResult("s3-b")],
+    )
+
+    root = app.AsyncResult("s3-bf-root")
+
+    assert dependency_ids(root) == [
+        (None, "s3-bf-root"),
+        ("s3-bf-root", "s3-a"),
+        ("s3-bf-root", "s3-b"),
+        ("s3-a", "s3-aa"),
+        ("s3-b", "s3-bb"),
+    ]
+    assert collect_ids(root, disable_sync_subtasks=False) == [
+        ("s3-bf-root", "ROOT"),
+        ("s3-a", "A"),

+        ("s3-aa", "AA"),
+        ("s3-bb", "BB"),

+    assert root.get_leaf() == "BB"

+
+def test_strict_iterdeps_raises_specific_incomplete_stream_for_pending_root():

+    store_success(app, "s3-ready-sibling-2", "ready-value")
+    store_success(
+        app,
+        "s3-root-started-child",
+        "root-value",

+            app.AsyncResult("s3-started-parent"),

+    parent, node = next(strict_stream)
+    assert (parent and parent.id, node.id) == (
+        "s3-root-started-child",
+        "s3-started-parent",
+    )

#!/bin/bash
set -e

cd /testbed

# Switch to Go 1.23 for compatibility with this older codebase
dev-switch go 1.23

# This is a pre-modules Go project using GOPATH with _vendor
export GO111MODULE=off
export GOPATH=/testbed/_vendor:/root/go
export CGO_ENABLED=1

# Ensure the project is available at the correct GOPATH import path
mkdir -p /testbed/_vendor/src/github.com/pingcap
ln -sf /testbed /testbed/_vendor/src/github.com/pingcap/tidb

# Build the parser (goyacc) and generate parser.go
make parser

# Fix invalid UTF-8 bytes in generated parser.go (goyacc emits 0xef 0xbf before final newline)
python3 -c "
with open('/testbed/parser/parser.go', 'rb') as f:
    data = f.read()
data = data.replace(b'\xef\xbf\n', b'\n')
with open('/testbed/parser/parser.go', 'wb') as f:
    f.write(data)
"

# Run the prepared test file
GO111MODULE=off GOPATH=/testbed/_vendor:/root/go CGO_ENABLED=1 \
  go test -p 3 -v github.com/pingcap/tidb/executor -check.f "TestPrepared|TestPreparedLimitOffset"

+		self.urgent = urgent

+    expect(nullResult).not.toContain('null')
